note: Where this file and a deposited register differ, the register governs.

claims.title: Natural Perception Hypothesis (NPH)
claims.claim: Natural selection acts on perceptual processing (the weighting, integration and stabilisation of sensory signals), and a heritable change in that processing changes which differences an organism can act on across contexts.
claims.falsifier: A heritable perceptual variant changes discrimination of its target signal class only, with no change in foraging, habitat use or mate choice under matched cue fields.

claims.title: Receiver-first evolution (RFE)
claims.claim: A heritable change in receiver sensory state, such as an opsin or odorant-receptor variant, starts divergence in mate choice and habitat preference while the focal cue field is held constant.
claims.falsifier: Lines differing only in the edited receiver gene show no divergence in mate choice or habitat preference under matched cue fields, or behaviour diverges only after cue-field divergence.

claims.title: Perception Ecology research programme
claims.claim: Perception Ecology is a research programme that studies how heritable, species-specific perceptual processing shapes ecological interaction and adaptive radiation, with the organism’s internal perceptual state as its first component.
claims.counts_against: A programme has no direct falsifier. Its standing rests on 1.1 and 2.2.

claims.title: Scope conditions for receiver-first routes
claims.claim: Receiver-first routes are worth testing where three conditions coincide. Receiver-state differences are repeatable or heritable, they redirect a behaviour with ecological reach, and that behaviour changes the cue, resource or reproductive environment later met by the same or descendant populations.
claims.counts_against: Receiver-first dynamics appear in systems where receiver differences are neither repeatable nor heritable, or where the behaviour has no ecological reach.

claims.title: Receiver-side pleiotropy: sensory-biased magic traits
claims.claim: One change in receiver perception couples ecological performance and mate choice, so the pleiotropy of a sensory-biased magic trait resides in the receiver rather than in the sender’s trait genes.
claims.falsifier: Swapping the sensory system between populations does not transfer both the preference and the performance difference.

claims.title: Primate trichromacy as candidate receiver-first loop
claims.claim: Primate trichromacy is a candidate receiver-first loop: an L/M opsin change improved red-green discrimination, shifted fruit choice, altered seed dispersal, and so changed selection on fruit colour and on colour vision.
claims.falsifier: Within polymorphic platyrrhine groups, trichromats and dichromats do not differ in choice of red-shifted fruit or in seed deposition; or fruit colour shows no association with primate vision after controlling for bird dispersers.

claims.title: Sensory-contrast restoration as conservation lever
claims.claim: Where turbidity, artificial light or noise collapses the sensory discrimination that maintains divergence, restoring sensory contrast protects the diverged populations more directly than managing habitat area.
claims.falsifier: Restoring contrast in a masked system does not restore assortative mating, or habitat-area management yields equal or larger recovery.

claims.title: Receiver-first as a frequency hypothesis
claims.claim: How often receiver-first routes operate is an empirical frequency question, decided system by system by four abandonment conditions. Receiver-first status is abandoned when prior receiver state fails to predict behaviour under matched conditions, when place history predicts behaviour better, when masking and rescue change nothing, or when environmental changes do not persist and return.
claims.counts_against: One condition met in a system removes receiver-first status for that system; across systems, the route is rare if most tested cases meet one.

claims.title: NPH amplification formalism
claims.claim: Because one sensory feature S enters the perception of every environmental trait (P_i = φ(S)·E_i), a small change in S shifts all perceived traits together and scales the selection gradient on S with the number of traits it touches.
claims.counts_against: A genetic change in one sensory feature (for example CFF) produces behavioural or fitness change no larger than a comparable single morphological change.

claims.title: Sensory-feedback loop model (RFE)
claims.claim: A path-coefficient loop model gives each link a named coefficient (Os→Oi γ, Oi→E α, E→Os and E→Oi returns, Oi→Os recalibration, Os inheritance via h² and β). “Which route operates” then becomes “which coefficients are non-zero”, estimable from designed toggles.
claims.counts_against: Os has low repeatability or heritability; initial Os fails to predict change in Oi under matched E; full-loop models do not outperform reduced ones in intact-loop blocks.

claims.title: Gated decomposition of receiver participation
claims.claim: A claim that a receiver change took part in an evolutionary process decomposes into five separately testable links, plus reproductive isolation for speciation, each tested against its simplest alternative. The links are receiver variation, discrimination difference, effect on action, ecological outcome and heritable component.
claims.counts_against: The receiver claim fails if general sensitivity change explains the difference, if receiver change does not alter generalisation, if categories do not transfer to new stimuli, if the effect vanishes after controls for learning, motivation and motor ability, or if action is unaffected.

claims.title: Gene-edit test of sensory-initiated divergence
claims.claim: Edit one opsin, phototransduction or odorant-receptor gene in Drosophila or a fish, hold the focal cue field within a tolerance band, and measure mate choice, habitat preference and environmental modification against unedited sibling controls.
claims.counts_against: Edited and control lines show no difference in mate choice, habitat preference or environmental modification under matched cue fields.

claims.title: Receiver-first niche construction motif
claims.claim: Receiver-first niche construction is the causal motif Os → Oi → E → (Os, Oi). Heritable receiver-state differences bias behaviour, the behaviour durably modifies the cue or resource field, and the modified field returns to affect later receiver state, performance or selection.
claims.falsifier: E does not diverge when feedback is enabled, or E diverges equally when masking removes Os-driven behavioural differences.

claims.title: Perceptual niche
claims.claim: A perceptual niche is the set of cue differences a given organism can register and act on; one measured habitat supports several perceptual niches, and a sensory variant defines a new one without any change in the measured habitat.
claims.falsifier: Variants that differ at a receptor locus show identical behavioural discrimination profiles over the habitat’s measured cue dimensions.

claims.title: Perceptual decline and ascent
claims.claim: Perceptual decline is the narrowing, coarsening or excessive cost of a range of differences formerly available to a lineage, and perceptual ascent is the appearance or sharpening of a discrimination. Both are defined on a stated axis and do not rank organisms.
claims.counts_against: The usage fails if decline and ascent on stated axes cannot be measured independently of each other.

claims.title: Eco-sensory triangle
claims.claim: Cue-mediated trait-environment matching is represented on one causal graph of E, Os and Oi, on which sensory drive, receiver bias, matching habitat choice and niche construction are constrained subgraphs. Holding, masking, encounter-equalising and feedback-toggling interventions diagnose the route that produced a match.
claims.falsifier: The stated interventions do not separate the motifs in simulation or experiment. Specific route claims also fail when Os differences are transient, modalities substitute under masking, or Oi → E changes do not persist.

claims.title: Used habitat as a collider
claims.claim: Where an organism is found is an outcome of preference, movement and sensory state, so conditioning analyses on realised habitat use manufactures phenotype-environment associations through collider stratification.
claims.falsifier: Phenotype-environment associations estimated conditional on use equal those from designs with assigned exposure.

claims.title: Minimal route model with structural zero
claims.claim: A three-state model X(t) = [E, Os, Oi] in which receiver state reaches E only through Oi (the structural zero ∂E(t+1)/∂Os(t) = 0) generates environment-first, receiver-first, sorting and feedback regimes from one set of equations.
claims.falsifier: Two regimes with similar endpoint matching are not separated by any intervention in the model, or durable E divergence appears under feedback-off.

claims.title: Cue-mediated magic-trait reporting standard
claims.claim: Every empirical magic-trait claim reports four elements: the phenotypic coupling route on the E-Os-Oi map, the architecture maintaining the association (pleiotropy or linkage), the evidence level (covariance, functional duality, causal manipulation, resolved architecture) and the coupling effect size.
claims.counts_against: Applying the standard to published cases changes none of their classifications relative to the existing magic/pseudomagic categories.

claims.title: Route-priority test
claims.claim: Receiver-led and sorting-led ordering are distinguished by whether prior receiver state Os(t) or a non-circular exposure proxy better predicts later Oi(t+1) out of sample under matched E, with the causal graph stated before model comparison.
claims.counts_against: Os(t) adds no out-of-sample prediction of Oi(t+1) beyond prior Oi and E_exp in a system claimed as receiver-led.

claims.title: Matched-field (flat-E) persistence test
claims.claim: If Oi divergence persists while the focal cue dimensions of E are held within a declared tolerance band over the decision window, a current-environment explanation of that divergence is rejected for those dimensions.
claims.counts_against: Divergence disappears under matched cue dimensions.

claims.title: Masking-rescue channel test
claims.claim: Reversibly masking and then restoring one sensory channel under matched conditions, with sham and general-impairment controls, identifies whether that channel carries Oi divergence; it does not identify the route that produced the divergence.
claims.counts_against: Divergence persists under verified masking of the channel.

claims.title: Three-link criterion for receiver-initiated feedback
claims.claim: Feedback counts as receiver-initiated only when Os predicts Oi under matched E, Oi durably modifies E or E_exp, and the modified conditions return to affect later Os, Oi, fitness or selection, tested with feedback-on/off blocks and standardised pulses.
claims.counts_against: E diverges at similar rates under feedback-on and feedback-off blocks.

claims.title: Encounter-equalisation test
claims.claim: Randomising settlement or equalising host, habitat, timing and encounter sequence tests sorting: matching or assortative mating that weakens while Os is unchanged was produced by non-random exposure.
claims.counts_against: Matching persists undiminished under verified encounter randomisation in a system claimed to be sorting-driven.

claims.title: 27-regime factorial intervention grammar
claims.claim: Holding each of E, Os and Oi high, low or free defines a 3 × 3 × 3 grammar of 27 regimes, of which the twelve two-fixed/one-free regimes are the clean local route tests.
claims.falsifier: An E-free module with Oi clamped still shows an Os effect on E that survives manipulation checks, or two-fixed/one-free contrasts reverse under difference-in-difference tests at the other level of the fixed factor.

claims.title: Host choice as receiver-first sorting
claims.claim: Sensory-driven adult host choice in phytophagous insects is receiver-first sorting, which redirects encounters without modifying the cue field; an Oi → E claim needs separate evidence that oviposition, larvae, microbes or substrate change durably alter the later environment.
claims.falsifier: Adult host choice alone produces durable change in the host cue field that returns to affect later host choice.

claims.title: Eco-sensory triangle SCM simulation
claims.claim: A VAR(1) structural causal model of E, Os and Oi, run under nine clamp/vary regimes including masking-rescue (γ_i suppressed then restored), recovers causal parameters by cross-lagged SEM and uses E_exp = E × sigmoid(Os) as its readout.
claims.counts_against: The masking-rescue regime fails to suppress and restore Oi divergence, or cross-lagged SEM fails to recover the generating coefficients.

claims.title: Evolution Canyon endogenous habitat-use design
claims.claim: At Israel’s Evolution Canyons, slope membership of mobile organisms results from movement, settlement and retention, so trait-environment effects there are identified only with measured exposure fields, assigned exposure histories and durability tests for feedback claims.
claims.falsifier: Trait-environment effects estimated from slope occupancy equal those from assigned-exposure designs for mobile EC taxa.

claims.title: Route-family classification result
claims.claim: Across 2,000 simulated datasets (400 per route family: receiver-first, environment-first, sorting-dominated, feedback, full-loop), held-out route classification was 44% from the observed pattern, 64% with flat-E, unchanged with masking, 77% with route asymmetry and 83% with feedback and post-pulse persistence.
claims.counts_against: A different model family or parameter range reverses the order of diagnostic value.

claims.title: Experienced cue stream E_exp
claims.claim: The experienced cue stream E_exp is a derived receiver-scale readout, not a fourth node, and is reported either as an exposure proxy built independently of Os or as a receiver-space model that does not count as evidence for Os.
claims.counts_against: Studies that violate the rule report Os effects no larger than studies that follow it.

claims.title: Spatial AMP: a heritable baseline calibration term
claims.claim: Perceived extent of an ecologically routed feature class decomposes as d’(C,s) = f0(C)·g(C,s)·d, and the evolutionary claim attaches only to the baseline term f0(C), never to the state term g.
claims.falsifier: A category-linked size-equivalence shift that disappears under state attenuation (satiation, octopamine block) or under feature matching, or that criterion, gain or lapse models fit as well across ≥3 anchors, refutes f0(C) ≠ 1 for that lineage.

claims.title: Adaptive Metric Perception: selection on equivalence structure
claims.claim: Selection under asymmetric ecological costs tunes the equivalence structure of perception: which physically different stimuli a lineage treats as equal, larger, nearer or faster, not only what enters a channel.
claims.falsifier: A proposed case fails if nuisance models absorb the effect, feature matching removes it, it fails to generalize across predicted anchors, or it changes response strength without changing the inferred equivalence function. At programme level, independent lineages with opposite cost asymmetries showing same-direction metric shifts count against AMP.

claims.title: Metric equivalence of physical-field and sensory-bias geometry
claims.claim: When a physical field and an organism’s sensory weighting field induce the same conformal metric ds^2 = n(x,y)2(dx2+dy^2), they yield identical Gaussian curvature and geodesics, so path structure alone cannot tell which generated the geometry.
claims.falsifier: Species tested over an identical layout show no reliable difference in fitted metric weighting n beyond detection differences, or behavioural paths are not predicted by geodesics of any fitted n.

claims.title: Metric leg and the transparency principle
claims.claim: A shared transformation of body and environment leaves unchanged every decision whose scale type it preserves: strictly increasing maps preserve ordinal decisions, positive affine maps preserve interval and norm-referenced decisions, and similarity maps preserve ratio decisions.
claims.falsifier: A reliable behavioral change under a verified shared transformation that lies inside the decision’s invariance class would refute it.

claims.title: Structured propagation of calibration bias
claims.claim: Under independent multiplicative log-gains ρ_x, ρ_t, ρ_m on extent, duration and mass, a derived quantity q = ∏x_j^a_j carries log bias Σa_jρ_j: velocity ρ_x − ρ_t, kinetic energy ρ_m + 2(ρ_x − ρ_t), time-to-contact ρ_t.
claims.falsifier: If all derived quantities shift by the same log amount, or velocity bias persists when independent estimates give ρ_x = ρ_t, the model fails.

claims.title: Acceleration bias depends on how velocity change is reconstructed
claims.claim: Under category-linked log-gains on perceptual primitives, perceived-acceleration bias is rho_dv - rho_t if velocity change is a primitive, rho_x - 2rho_t if derived from displacement over time, and a cue-geometry function if inferred from looming, so matched space-time gains cancel velocity bias but not derived acceleration bias.
claims.falsifier: Acceleration judgments under matched space-time gains show no residual bias of -rho_t, and no delta-v model fits better than the velocity-based expression.

claims.title: Interaction creates a local ground truth for cross-species calibration
claims.claim: Observers with different time scales can agree on time, speed and acceleration only through a shared third reference, and every physical interaction (with a floor, a mate, a food item) supplies such a local ground truth.
claims.falsifier: If organisms with shifted temporal resolution show no calibration change after contact events (e.g. no update of interception timing after landing or capture), the thesis fails.

claims.title: Coupled Perceptual Recalibration
claims.claim: Exposure-induced shifts in feature-specific calibration move self and other representations together, with directed transfer G_{b←a}^{(c,τ)} = Δθ_b/Δθ_a, and population preference divergence produces assortative mating only when preferred signal distributions covary with exposure regimes.
claims.falsifier: Preregistered transfer thresholds are not met, or exposure regime and preferred signal distributions do not covary.

claims.title: Local calibration to the encountered distribution
claims.claim: Perceptual metrics such as heavy, far and fast are set relative to the distribution of values an organism encounters, so a controlled shift of that distribution moves the reference point by a predicted direction and amount.
claims.falsifier: If the experienced distribution is shifted and the reference point does not move, or moves opposite to the prediction, the hypothesis fails in that case.

claims.title: Multi-anchor discriminator: remapping versus criterion shift
claims.claim: Metric remapping predicts a log-scale PSE shift that is constant across anchors, while an additive criterion shift predicts a log-scale shift ln((s+α)/s) that falls with the standard s; the two coincide at a single anchor.
claims.counts_against: Across ≥3 anchors spanning a preregistered range, a fitted log shift that follows ln((s+α)/s), or remapping failing to beat additive, gain and lapse models by the preregistered ΔAIC/ELPD margin, rejects remapping for that dataset.

claims.title: Evidential ladder for metric-tuning claims
claims.claim: A metric-tuning claim advances through nine ordered evidential steps, and each step names what it rules out and what it leaves open.
claims.counts_against: A demonstrated metric-tuning case in which a lower step (for example, state attenuation) fails while the higher steps hold would show the ordering is wrong.

claims.title: Drosophila size-equivalence falsification programme
claims.claim: Measure size-equivalence of neutral discs, threat-like silhouettes and feature-matched non-threat controls across ≥3 anchors in Drosophila, then test state attenuation, bidirectional selection on the normalized remapping parameter ρ, and upstream visual readouts.
claims.counts_against: An effect that appears only as higher escape probability or shorter latency, or that fails any of the five go/no-go criteria, is scored as not spatial AMP.

claims.title: Causal-route controls for metric claims
claims.claim: Four control contrasts classify a metric shift as receiver-led, environment-led, sorting-led or feedback-amplified: matched external cues, reversible sensory-route perturbation with rescue, receiver-state versus encounter-history prediction, and feedback-reset versus feedback-enabled regimes.
claims.counts_against: A shift that persists after reversible route perturbation, or that encounter history predicts better than receiver state, is classified as not receiver-led.

claims.title: Local invasion condition for spatial remapping
claims.claim: In a signal-detection model with imperfect routing (r_P > r_N), remapping f > 1 invades from neutrality exactly when λπ_P r_P E_P[dφ((d−θ)/σ)] exceeds κπ_N r_N E_N[dφ((d−θ)/σ)].
claims.counts_against: Within the model the result is analytic. Empirically, a lineage with informative routing and a high miss/false-alarm cost ratio that shows no baseline expansion (f0 ≈ 1) after state control counts against the model’s relevance. So does a lineage where a threshold shift alone reaches the same fitness.

claims.title: The ruler problem
claims.claim: A manual measurement is a perceived target/standard ratio, so its log bias is ρ_target − ρ_standard: category remapping cancels when target and standard share a calibration class and yields a bias factor exp(ρ_target − ρ_standard) when they do not.
claims.falsifier: If measurement bias is equal in same-category and cross-category conditions, or a global-gain model fits cross-category data as well as remapping, the ruler model fails for that observer.

claims.title: Measurement inheritance through observer-calibrated pipelines
claims.claim: In a two-population model, selection on receiver calibration propagates into a measurement pipeline in proportion to its observer-derived calibration weight κ, and vanishes under external calibration.
claims.falsifier: If population-calibrated pipelines agree across populations as closely as externally calibrated ones, or divergence does not scale with κ, the model fails.

claims.title: Design identifiability boundary for AMP
claims.claim: In simulation, the archived three-anchor design recovers canonical remapping (ρ_P = 0.139) decisively in 21.7% of 60 datasets, while candidate_B (five anchors, ±0.50 log offsets, 60 trials per cell) does so in 96.8% of 500 datasets with mean bias −0.0002.
claims.counts_against: A rerun of candidate_B with the shipped code and seeds that yields decisive recovery below 80% or |bias| above 0.03 at ρ_P = 0.139 would overturn the result.

claims.title: Label-mediated transfer of population bias to a classifier
claims.claim: In simulation, a per-pixel classifier trained on segmentation labels from an evolved population carries that population’s measurement shift: area bias 0.30 and 0.13 for two population-trained classifiers against 0.79 for a ground-truth-trained control.
claims.counts_against: If population-trained and ground-truth-trained classifiers show the same area bias across more seeds, the transfer is not supported.

claims.title: Task-success selection yields measurement bias
claims.claim: In simulation, selection acting only on success in three ecological tasks produced a stable negative bias in an unrewarded rod-length readout (−8% protected rod, −14% vulnerable rod) through sensory parameters shared by the tasks and the readout.
claims.counts_against: If shuffled-fitness, no-selection or policy-only arms reproduce the tight negative bias, the selection explanation fails.

claims.title: Adversarial failure map for AMP
claims.claim: With ρ_P = 0 by construction, candidate_B’s joint model falsely supports remapping above 5% for 2 of 17 adversarial truths, and a category-P low-level stimulus mismatch above 0.02 log units breaks identifiability.
claims.counts_against: A rerun giving false joint support above 5% for further truths, or safe offsets above 0.05, would change the design rule.

claims.title: Experiential Field Selection (EFS)
claims.claim: Selection acts on the sensory, bodily, interoceptive and sensorimotor architecture that draws the operational body-world partition, not on experience or the partition itself.
claims.counts_against: The category outcomes are conditionally independent given internal state, detection and motor capacity; EFS then reduces to a descriptive synthesis.

claims.title: Partition precedes metric
claims.claim: A distinction must be stabilized (EFS) before selection can tune metric equivalence within it (Adaptive Metric Perception).
claims.falsifier: A lineage shows selected metric equivalence along a dimension it does not partition.

claims.title: Pre-partition and membrane-first origin
claims.claim: The partition originates in a membrane plus chemotaxis and reafference, before any perceiving subject; before it is drawn, the cue stream is not sorted for the organism into body, object, route, threat or background.
claims.falsifier: Body-object distinctions appear in lineages lacking the reafferent control that the account places before them.

claims.title: Organismal regulation preserves its own regulating process
claims.claim: Stars and organisms both regulate; a star’s feedback preserves a balance of forces, while an organism’s feedback preserves the conditions without which the regulating process itself stops.
claims.falsifier: A non-living system whose feedback preserves the conditions of its own regulating process in the same closed way.

claims.title: Body-world boundary set by a temporal binding window
claims.claim: Signals integrable within the organism’s multisensory temporal binding window are assigned to the body, so baseline temporal acuity predicts the visuomotor delay at which body ownership breaks.
claims.falsifier: No correlation between baseline temporal acuity and the ownership-breaking delay, or no extension of delay tolerance in tool experts.

claims.title: Coupled repartitioning across action categories
claims.claim: Under a matched cue field, a change in receiver state or architecture reorganizes reachability, defensive threshold, route, shelter, social spacing and body-near contact together, as one partition not reducible to a single latent state.
claims.falsifier: Behaviours are conditionally independent given measured latent state, detection and motor capacity, or loadings are invariant across niches.

claims.title: Body as first object: reafference mutual information
claims.claim: The self-cluster is the part of the sensory stream with the highest joint mutual information with action-contingent reafference and interoceptive state.
claims.falsifier: The privileged self-cluster tracks stimulus salience rather than contingency.

claims.title: Field grammar and three fingerprints
claims.claim: Selection tunes the grammar by which an organism sorts its field into functional roles, detectable by target-standard cancellation, lawful propagation into derived judgements, and co-warp of body-anchored judgements by one body-scale term.
claims.counts_against: Fear, arousal, hunger, motor ability or task strategy explain the pattern as well as the body-scale term.

claims.title: Conditional-independence null for repartitioning
claims.claim: Coupled repartitioning is tested against the null that category outcomes are conditionally independent given measured internal state, detection and motor capacity.
claims.counts_against: Residual partial correlations are zero after partialling out (s, d, m).

claims.title: Proto-body
claims.claim: The proto-body is a minimal self-model with three components: a boundary estimate, an internal-condition vector and a controllability map.
claims.counts_against: Every manipulation moves all three components together.

claims.title: Receiver-relative trait reorganization (RRT)
claims.claim: A measured change in a receiver’s sensory-organizational mapping (R, Π) reorganizes the task-relative units through which existing physical variation affects action, creating new dimensions of selection before matching physical traits evolve.
claims.falsifier: Independently measured receiver change fails to predict the equivalence structure; or a simpler sensitivity, criterion, exposure or motor model predicts it as well; or the receiver pathway adds nothing to the combined model.

claims.title: Enviro-Type and speciation rate
claims.claim: Clades whose members differ in more heritable receiver-field configurations (Enviro-Types) speciate faster, after phylogenetic control.
claims.falsifier: No correlation between Enviro-Type count or sensory-gene diversity and speciation rate after phylogenetic control.

claims.title: Three-times model
claims.claim: Receiver reorganization at t_1 changes the interaction phenotype at once without change to peripheral morphology; at t_2 the altered behaviour can change heritable variants, so receiver reorganization precedes and redirects morphological evolution.
claims.falsifier: Receiver reorganization never precedes morphological change in lineages where both are tracked.

claims.title: Three-component receiver-relative organization
claims.claim: Receiver-relative organization decomposes into registered metric m, probabilistic attribution α and functional co-membership Π, supported only if the multicomponent model beats decision-only, common-factor, metric-only, attribution-only and continuous-coupling models on new observations and selective perturbations.
claims.counts_against: The multicomponent model fails to beat the named alternatives on held-out action and perturbation data.

claims.title: Effective-phenotype formal chain
claims.claim: Φ_eff = {U, T, Rel, Bound} is produced from stimulus S(t), body state B and history H through R, Π and Ψ, and action, consequences and fitness follow from Φ_eff.
claims.counts_against: The partition model fails to outperform the fixed-trait and sampling-only competitors.

claims.title: Task-equivalence criterion for trait origination
claims.claim: Strong trait origination is credited only if an independently measured receiver change prospectively predicts a split, merge or boundary shift of task-equivalence classes, confirmed on held-out stimuli beyond sensitivity, criterion, exposure, attention and motor accounts.
claims.counts_against: Any of the four conditions fails.

claims.title: Extended-system unit test
claims.claim: A body plus tool, or host plus symbiont, counts as one functional unit only if the integrated model predicts held-out data better than the body alone, the link survives a change of measure, and the system fails at stated thresholds.
claims.counts_against: The integrated system does not fail at the stated thresholds, or the integrated model does not beat the body-alone model.

claims.title: Underground-hand thought experiment and combined causal test
claims.claim: Under matched physical sources, two independently estimated receiver mappings yield different performance surfaces and selection gradients on the same appendage variants, and RRT is supported only if the receiver pathway adds out-of-sample prediction in a combined direct-plus-mediated model.
claims.counts_against: The two mappings yield the same performance surface, or the mediated path adds no held-out prediction.

claims.title: Effective phenotype
claims.claim: The effective phenotype is the realized organization, at a declared level and time window, of the units, boundaries, properties and relations that a receiver-body-environment system makes functionally available, split into available and recruited parts.
claims.counts_against: A partition model fails to explain generalization data that fixed-trait and sampling-only models cannot.

claims.title: Six kinds of effective-phenotype change
claims.claim: Effective-phenotype change comes in six kinds, value, attribution, boundary, individuation, dimension and relation, and only changes that cannot be written as a monotone transform of a predefined variable count as strong novelty.
claims.falsifier: Every observed receiver change fits a monotone transform of a predefined variable.

claims.title: Organizational architecture φ as the candidate phenotype
claims.claim: Organizational architecture φ = (θ, κ, ψ, λ) is the set of stage parameters of a registration-grouping-labelling transformation that produces realized organization O = (m, Π, α), and φ, not O, is the candidate organism-borne phenotype.
claims.falsifier: Peripheral, common-factor, decision-criterion or continuous-similarity models predict held-out behaviour as well as the staged model.

claims.title: Sensorimotor repartitioning
claims.claim: An independently measured change in how an organism localizes and controls a body field prospectively predicts new functional variation, and becomes a target of selection before an external-surface protocol detects a matching morphological boundary.
claims.counts_against: The gradient model predicts as well as the discrete model; q changes without any change in action; or total gain, attention or generic learning explains the effects.

claims.title: Selection gradient on q
claims.claim: Repartitioning becomes evolutionary through three staged links, functional variation in q, selection on q via performance, and response given heritable q, with a nonzero selection gradient on q after sensitivity, size, strength and learning rate are controlled.
claims.falsifier: q is not heritable, or shows no selection gradient after controls.

claims.title: Partition strength q
claims.claim: Partition strength q_i is the held-out ELPD gain of a two-region model with a training-estimated boundary over the better of a one-region model and a flexible continuous-gradient model.
claims.counts_against: q ≤ 0 in organisms with an independently established partition.

claims.title: Appendage partition criteria
claims.claim: A functional partition of an externally continuous appendage requires convergence of five criteria, regional heterogeneity, dual localization, differential loading, differential action and perturbation-specific persistence, plus cross-validated superiority of the two-region model.
claims.counts_against: A claimed partition yields no out-of-sample or causal consequence.

claims.title: Octopus-arm and haltere programme
claims.claim: In octopus arms, discrete-joint models are compared with smooth-curvature models on held-out reaching kinematics; in Drosophila halteres, a two-field model of campaniform sensilla is compared with a smooth field and genotype-level q is tested against flight performance.
claims.counts_against: Two-region models do not outperform smooth models, or haltere q does not predict flight performance.

claims.title: Simulation operating range of q
claims.claim: In simulation with 400 trials per individual, q > 2 detects a true two-region field in 96.7% of individuals, with false-positive rates of 0.020 under one region, 0.093 under a linear gradient and 0.167 under a steep smooth sigmoid.
claims.counts_against: Generic gain or noise changes produce q > 2 at rates near the true-partition rate.

claims.title: Protocol-indexed units
claims.claim: Unit claims are indexed to property, protocol, task and purpose; external-surface, physiological, sensorimotor, behavioural and developmental protocols return different partitions of the same body part, compared as full partitions, not counts.
claims.counts_against: The claim fails if a division disappears under blinded replication, fails to generalize, or adds no predictive value.

claims.title: The organism–field coupling is the interactor
claims.claim: Within the scientific description, the interactor is the organism coupled to its perceived and enacted field, and the replicator is the heritable receiver architecture.
claims.counts_against: Fitness is predicted as well by independent, trait-by-trait receiver parameters as by the coupled organism–field partition, so the coupling adds no interactor-level cohesion.

claims.title: Category-boundary location is an individual phenotype
claims.claim: We treat the location of a categorical boundary as an individual reaction-norm phenotype, with repeatability, plasticity, additive-genetic variance and a fitness effect that standard designs can estimate.
claims.counts_against: Repeated measurement shows b_i is not repeatable within individuals; or half-sib or selection-line designs with power at least 0.8 for h2 = 0.1 bound Var_A(b_i) below that value; or male mating success shows no dependence on boundary straddling at matched physical distance (gamma = 0).

claims.title: Calibration shields boundary location from selection
claims.claim: In the reaction norm b_ij = (1-w_i)g_i + w_i m_ij + p_i + e_ij, selection moves the mean boundary by (1-w)^2 sigma2_g beta, and a heritable calibration weight w lets selection act on the learning rule whenever m differs from mean g.
claims.falsifier: A selection-line experiment on a categorical boundary in which the realized response departs from (1-w)^2 sigma2_g beta given independently estimated w and sigma2_g; or a boundary that evolves beyond m under selection on the learning rule alone.

claims.title: No generation count clears non-genetic transmission
claims.claim: Common-garden rearing for any number of generations does not exclude non-genetic transmission; separating genetic from non-genetic inheritance requires design (reciprocal crosses, cross-fostering, pedigree-based additive variance), and even then shows transmitted variation, not selection.
claims.counts_against: A demonstration that a fixed number of common-garden generations removes all listed non-genetic channels in a given system. That would restrict the claim to other systems.

claims.title: Labelling-plus-discrimination rule separates boundary shifts from criterion shifts
claims.claim: A boundary shift is diagnosed only when the discrimination peak moves with the labelling boundary, and a preregistered confidence-bound rule classified no true boundary shift as a criterion shift in 14,400 simulated replicates.
claims.falsifier: Empirical data in which a single decision-criterion parameter reproduces both the labelling shift and a moved discrimination peak; or a simulation variant (for example a non-Gaussian peak) in which the rule misclassifies boundary shifts as criterion shifts above 5%.

claims.title: Drosophila serrata boundary protocol
claims.claim: We specify a Drosophila serrata contact-pheromone protocol that first tests whether a categorical boundary exists and then estimates its heritability in a family-level half-sib design of about 10^4 singly tested females, followed by divergent selection on boundary location.
claims.counts_against: No sharp labelling function with a discrimination peak at stage 0; or a sire component whose upper 95% limit excludes h2 = 0.1 at power >= 0.8, together with no response to five generations of divergent selection.

claims.title: Split-brood tutoring separates intrinsic location, calibration and learning rule
claims.claim: A two-origin by two-tutor split-brood design maps intrinsic location onto an origin effect, calibration onto a tutor effect, and a population difference in learning rule onto an origin-by-tutor interaction; in swamp sparrows 12-20 nests per population detect an intrinsic component equal to half the reported population difference.
claims.counts_against: A tutor effect equal to the population difference, with no origin effect and no interaction, at power at least 0.9 for w = 0.5, falsifies an intrinsic difference. An origin effect equal to the population difference with no tutor effect falsifies calibration. An interaction identifies the learning rule as the differing phenotype.

claims.title: Equal-ratio intervals are discriminated unequally by Pennsylvania swamp sparrows
claims.claim: Pennsylvania swamp sparrows failed the 8-to-16 ms doubling, which crosses the New York boundary, and succeeded on the 16-to-32 ms doubling, which crosses their own; under ratio coding the two are equally hard, so we propose that boundary position, not ratio size, set the outcome.
claims.counts_against: A duration-coding model with a generalized Weber law (noise s.d. = kt + c) fitted to swamp-sparrow duration discrimination that reproduces failure at 8-to-16 ms and success at 16-to-32 ms without a boundary; or a within-population test in which equal-ratio pairs on one side of the boundary are discriminated unequally.

claims.title: Two estimation biases for boundary location
claims.claim: Fixing the lapse rate at zero pulls estimated boundaries toward the centre of the stimulus range at any trial number, and treating estimated boundaries as data attenuates repeatability by up to 37% in the simulated conditions, so latent boundaries must be fitted jointly with the psychometric response.
claims.falsifier: Joint fitting with an explicit lapse model that fails to remove the centre-ward bias; or repeatability estimated from boundary point estimates that matches latent repeatability at 24 trials and shallow spread.

claims.title: No recorded estimate of heritability of a categorical boundary
claims.claim: A recorded OpenAlex search of 1329 unique records (18 queries plus forward citations of six founding studies, 15 September 2026) found no estimate of repeatability, additive-genetic variance, twin concordance, response to selection or common-garden persistence for the location of a boundary shown to be categorical.
claims.falsifier: Any published estimate of repeatability, heritability, twin concordance, selection response or common-garden persistence for the location of a boundary that meets the labelling-plus-discrimination criterion.

claims.title: Perceptual ontology (narrowed NPH)
claims.claim: Species-specific sensory ecologies shape perceptual ontology, the organism-relative units, boundaries, events and relations first available for action, and perceptual ontology sets the entry conditions for proto-logical cognition without determining formal logic or mathematics.
claims.counts_against: Raw count predicts early quantity judgements as well as grouping variables do, or cross-modal transfer tracks magnitude rather than shared segmentation.

claims.title: Individuation without a privileged partition
claims.claim: Where a quantity depends on an individuation criterion that no independent procedure validates, agreement among procedures does not identify a privileged partition; where fitness passes through a receiver, selection acts on the partition that receiver produces.
claims.falsifier: A validated independent procedure that selects one partition of the track surfaces; or a receiver-mediated selection case in which fitness tracks an analyst-defined unit the receiver does not separate.

claims.title: Unit change preserves the measurand; individuation change need not
claims.claim: A lawful change of unit preserves the measurand and its relevant relations, whereas a change in the criterion of individuation (one organism, one species, one event) can change the population, the variable and the inference, so units and targets are stabilised by different regimes.
claims.falsifier: Systematic cases in which a change of individuation criterion leaves every downstream estimate and inference invariant, as a unit change does.

claims.title: Spatiotemporal grain: advantage belongs to the encounter
claims.claim: A receiver’s spatiotemporal grain (temporal resolution, integration window, response latency, spatial resolution, range) is a multidimensional phenotype whose advantage belongs to the encounter, so swapping the opponent or the lighting changes the ranking of advantage while individual capacities stay fixed.
claims.falsifier: Advantage rankings stay the same across opponents and lighting conditions after hunger, experience, terrain and motivation are controlled.

claims.title: Stevens’s law, not only Weber’s law, prices exaggeration
claims.claim: Sensory ecology adopted Weber’s law of discriminability without Stevens’s power law of magnitude, and proportional processing alone does not limit ornament exaggeration: the limit inferred since Cohen (1984) comes from pricing cost in absolute units and benefit in proportional units.
claims.falsifier: A bisection or magnitude-estimation assay in a signalling receiver that gives an area exponent equal to the length exponent; or a model in which proportional processing alone, with cost and benefit in the same units, bounds exaggeration.

claims.title: Counts have no physical standard, so evolved individuation shifts escape instrumental correction
claims.claim: Unit counts are the derived quantity without a physical standard, so instruments cannot correct an evolved shift in individuation, and a shift fixed across a population leaves no reference class to detect it.
claims.falsifier: A physical standard that fixes unit counts without an individuation criterion; or a population-fixed individuation shift detected by an instrument without a receiver-defined partition.

claims.title: Receiver cascade: separability is stage-dependent
claims.claim: The receiver transforms a phenotype through at least five stages (projection, sampling, segmentation or integration, magnitude scaling, comparison); a trait can be behaviourally separable at one stage and not at the next, so selection gradients on analyst-defined components misassign the causal route when behaviour reads an integrated projected-area variable.
claims.falsifier: Orthogonal manipulation of component area, total projected area, boundary contrast and configuration in which females show component-specific preference at fixed total area.

claims.title: Event number is indexed to temporal grain
claims.claim: The number of events in a sequence has no receiver-free value: a 40 Hz flicker is forty events per second for a receiver whose flicker-fusion frequency exceeds 40 Hz and one steady light for a receiver whose fusion frequency is lower.
claims.falsifier: Animals discriminate event counts reliably at flicker rates above their measured fusion frequency.

claims.title: Strategic animacy: relevance shifts animacy under stimulus-matched cues
claims.claim: Relevance or control-demand manipulations shift animacy and agency judgments under stimulus-matched motion cues, through top-down priors and precision at the object layer.
claims.falsifier: Animacy ratings do not change with relevance or control demand when motion statistics are held identical.

claims.title: Receiver-shaped route to mathematics
claims.claim: The order in which an organism reaches mathematical concepts follows its individuation format: object-partitioning receivers reach the discrete unit first, and field-sensing receivers such as weakly electric fish reach continuous composition first.
claims.falsifier: Electrosensory tasks in weakly electric fish acquire discrete-count rules as fast as or faster than matched continuous-gradient rules, with stimulus difficulty equated.

claims.title: Individuation format precedes quantity and counting
claims.claim: We propose that the format of individuation (spatial partition for objects, temporal grain for events) is an evolved precondition of quantity discrimination and counting, and we test it through three predictions on non-numerical cues, segmentation and cross-format generalisation.
claims.falsifier: Any of the three predictions failing in a species with a characterised perceptual space; for example, matched non-numerical cues leave numerical effects unchanged.

claims.title: The exponent is not identifiable in two-choice assays; bisection identifies it
claims.claim: In two-choice preference assays the psychophysical exponent beta enters only as the product f’ x beta and is not identifiable, whereas a bisection assay with small and large anchors gives PSE = ((a_s^beta + a_lbeta)/2)(1/beta), which identifies beta.
claims.falsifier: A two-choice design that recovers beta separately from f’; or bisection data whose PSEs across anchor ratios fit no single beta.

claims.title: Known-maker calibration protocol for trace reconstruction
claims.claim: We specify a known-maker protocol that uses a guineafowl track with synchronized biplanar X-ray digit trajectories (XMAPortal GFLAR07RUN03) as ground truth to score detection, partition, boundary and identity error across seven representations read by experts, novices and algorithms.
claims.counts_against: Reconstruction errors on the known-maker track do not differ across representations. That would show that representation sensitivity does not become reconstruction error.

claims.title: Low-frequency attenuation adds regions to footprint partitions in a dose-dependent way
claims.claim: On 37 published track surfaces, attenuating low spatial frequencies with a filter pair identical above a transition frequency increases the number of recovered regions on 28 surfaces and decreases it on none, and the increase grows with attenuation on 36 of 37.
claims.falsifier: A null or non-monotone dose-response across surfaces; or a gain in regions accompanied by a change in selected area, which would make the effect a thresholding artefact.

claims.title: Illumination azimuth changes and reorders footprint partitions
claims.claim: On 37 track surfaces, illumination azimuth alone changes the recovered region count on every surface (median span x2.20, up to x7.0), light along the specimen’s principal axis recovers more regions on 31 of 37, and specimen rankings reverse in 26.2% of surface-pair comparisons.
claims.falsifier: A reanalysis with an independent decoder or human outliners in which along-axis light does not recover more regions, or in which rankings are stable across azimuth.

claims.title: Swordtail reanalysis: proportional processing is not identified
claims.claim: In the archived Caves & Kelley (2023) swordtail data, proportional processing is not identified: the two-fan design correlates the proportional difference with the smaller male’s area (r = -0.78), two untested predictors fit as well, and a Box-Cox contrast excludes all three published models.
claims.counts_against: A factorial design that varies small-stimulus size and ratio independently and finds preference tracks the ratio at fixed smaller-male area.

claims.title: Receiver-envelope sensitivity of footprint partitions
claims.claim: Across 1,949 DinoTracker footprint silhouettes, reducing spatial access through a graded series of receiver envelopes changes the number of connected regions monotonically, from 2.3% of silhouettes under a Homo-Pan LCA envelope to 24.6% under a compound-eye comparator.
claims.falsifier: A partition-change rate that is flat or non-monotone across the envelope series, or that vanishes when the same envelopes are applied to raw surfaces of known-maker tracks.

claims.title: Four-level individuation hierarchy and connectedness-continuity conflict
claims.claim: Sensory individuation has four levels (segmentation, reidentification, generalization, inference), and its organism-relative character is tested by placing a stipulated material relation in conflict with a measured modality-specific continuity cue.
claims.falsifier: Classification tracks material connectedness, not electrosensory continuity, when the two conflict.

claims.title: Proto-logic
claims.claim: Proto-logic is a class of prelinguistic, nonformal expectations about relations (identity and difference, one-many, part-whole, containment, support, contact causation) that operate on already individuated units, support comparison and expectation, and remain approximate.
claims.falsifier: Expectations of the listed relation types appear before the organism individuates the relevant units.

claims.title: Token-directed sensory individuation and electric-fish reviewing test
claims.claim: Sensory individuation is the establishment of a task-usable target unit to which later information is attributed selectively, tested in weakly electric fish by an object-specific reviewing design with position exchange.
claims.counts_against: No same-target advantage after position exchange with matched final displays, or behaviour fully predicted by location or carrier models.

claims.title: Receiver-Calibration Selection
claims.claim: Heritable variation in a few receiver-calibration parameters θ (spectral, temporal, gain) changes many receiver-mediated interactions at once, so selection from any of them loads onto the same parameters: β_θ = Σ_j (∂ln w/∂y_j)(∂y_j/∂θ).
claims.falsifier: If the effective dimensionality of G across the task battery approaches the number of tasks, or selection through one receiver task produces no correlated response in unselected tasks sharing the parameter, RCS is wrong as formulated.

claims.title: Enrichment of receiver-calibration alleles in selectional-pleiotropy space
claims.claim: Receiver-calibration alleles are enriched in the high-magnitude, high-breadth region of the selectional-pleiotropy profile (A_g, B_g, K_g) relative to matched regulatory, neural, endocrine and developmental loci.
claims.falsifier: After matching for effect size, expression breadth, network position and viability, receiver-calibration alleles show no higher B_g than matched non-receiver loci.

claims.title: Brake-and-accelerator tempo hypothesis
claims.claim: A stable receiver-calibration regime buffers the effective environment and yields bounded fluctuation, while rare calibration-regime shifts move many selective optima at once; multi-trait bursts therefore coincide with documented sensory-regime transitions more often than under independence.
claims.falsifier: Burst timing is statistically independent of sensory-system transitions in sister-clade contrasts.

claims.title: Perceptual grouping predicts correlational selection
claims.claim: Independently measured perceptual grouping Π_ab of two signal components predicts the correlational selection gradient γ_ab that the receiver imposes, after chemical or physical similarity, biosynthetic pathway and total emission are fitted.
claims.falsifier: Π does not predict γ once chemical class and biosynthesis are fitted; valuation is separable wherever grouping is strong; or Π is not repeatable under fixed experience.

claims.title: Assimilation test for receiver calibration
claims.claim: After multi-generation selection under a stable altered sensory regime, descendants reared in both regimes show a flatter reaction norm of calibration, not only a shifted mean.
claims.falsifier: Means shift while the reaction-norm slope is unchanged across regimes.

claims.title: Receiver-to-G status ledger
claims.claim: The chain from source properties to genetic covariance has eleven links, each labelled established, unmeasured, non-identifiable, definitional, unknown or conditional, and the weight-bearing untested link is grouping → joint valuation.
claims.falsifier: A null difference in non-additivity between grouping-trained and control bees (, corrected design) falsifies link 7 and removes links 8–11.

claims.title: Within-species grouping manipulation
claims.claim: Induce configural versus elemental treatment of the same odour pair in bees by training, confirm the difference with three non-preference assays, then estimate the product term of the unrewarded free-flight valuation surface; the grouping arm shows the larger product term.
claims.falsifier: The product term does not differ between arms at a preregistered detectable effect size.

claims.title: Feasibility audit: perceptual data are the limiting resource
claims.claim: A test of grouping-predicts-covariance on published data is blocked: none of the twelve Brassica rapa volatiles with an estimated G matrix (Zu et al. 2020) appears in the 16-odorant honeybee generalization panel (Guerrieri et al. 2005), and the broadest floral panel shares two.
claims.counts_against: A published perceptual-similarity dataset covering the Brassica volatiles would remove the block.

claims.title: Target-artifact gap
claims.claim: A reproducible access product can stabilize an operational relation that differs from the target relation its claim asserts. Overinterpretation enters at the operational-to-target step, which statistical, risk-of-bias, metrological and reporting review leave unexamined.
claims.counts_against: In a sample of retracted or corrected empirical claims, the decisive error lies mostly in data production (fabrication, faulty measurement, statistical error), not in the operational-to-target step.

claims.title: Non-automatic claim-status inheritance and residual claims
claims.claim: Warrant does not pass automatically from a result to a transformed claim. Content reused for a different target, relation or strength needs its warrant re-established, and the audit outputs the strongest residual claim that survives.
claims.counts_against: In a sample of cited claims, strength-changing transitions without a named invariance hold up under later tests as often as transitions with one.

claims.title: Route-relative robustness and dependency-diverse support
claims.claim: Replication counts against a suspected artifact only when it changes, bounds or independently tests the dependency that artifact route runs through; replication along the same laboratory, reagent, cell line or pipeline reproduces the artifact as readily as the target.
claims.falsifier: A set of cases in which replication along a shared dependency exposed the suspected artifact as often as dependency-diverse replication did.

claims.title: Stability under dataset swaps sets evidential status
claims.claim: The status of a cosmological model preference is set by its stability under swaps of dataset combination, calibration treatment and model assumptions, not by a sigma threshold borrowed from particle physics.
claims.counts_against: Across historical cosmological claims, peak single-combination significance predicts later confirmation as well as minimum-across-swaps significance does.

claims.title: Access-path attribution grammar
claims.claim: A measured difference is attributed to a target only after its access path is specified and compared with alternative paths; attribution is licensed where the target’s sensitivity direction lies outside the span of the path’s sensitivity directions, and what survives path substitution is credited to the target.
claims.counts_against: Across the worked cases, the grammar never classifies a claim differently from current practice and never blocks an inference that was actually made.

claims.title: Diagnostic Access Correction Framework (DACF)
claims.claim: DACF audits a single empirical claim by separating what its access chain stabilized from the target relation the claim asserts, and ends every audit with a written corrected claim: stand, narrow, qualify or refuse.
claims.counts_against: In the reviewer study, DACF corrected claims converge no better, and match historical resolutions no better, than ordinary prose reviews of the same cases.

claims.title: Microscopy claim-dependency record
claims.claim: The microscopy claim-dependency record rewrites an imaging conclusion into minimal propositions and passes each through two gates: whether the image operation is validated for its measurement task, and which biological proposition that validated operation warrants.
claims.counts_against: In the blinded comparison, coders cannot apply dependency groups consistently, dependency maps do not change synthesis conclusions, or a simpler method reaches the same calibration with less burden.

claims.title: Claim-level audit for sensory ecology
claims.claim: The sensory-ecology claim audit codes each claim instance by biological target level, assertive force and evidence route, and outputs preserved, narrowed, out of scope or unsupported escalation, together with the residual claim the evidence licenses.
claims.counts_against: Independent coders on a predefined claim sample disagree on target level or output so often that the residual claim is not reproducible (for example, Krippendorff’s α below 0.67 on the output category).

claims.title: XMRV/ME-CFS worked reconstruction
claims.claim: A DACF reconstruction of XMRV and ME/CFS keeps the operational history, that access chains produced XMRV-like signals more often in patient samples, and refuses the infection claim, because admissible contamination routes were never separated from infection.
claims.falsifier: The historical record shows that positive studies used contamination-independent routes (mouse-DNA-free reagents, independent cell lines) and still detected XMRV.

claims.title: Route-aware reading of image-based profiling
claims.claim: A route-aware reading of eleven image-based profiling studies supports perturbation-associated image variation, makes phenotype identity conditional on batch separation, and supports a unique target or mechanism only where a molecular or prospective functional anchor changed the route.
claims.counts_against: In the cross-laboratory design, retrieval for a nominated target weakens under technical separation, or maps to generic stress responses instead of prespecified functional endpoints.

claims.title: Claim-audit pilot results
claims.claim: In a single-coder purposive pilot of 13 claim instances from 11 sensory-ecology papers, six were preserved, five narrowed and two routed out of scope. The narrowings fell at the step from sensory mechanism to behavioural or evolutionary consequence.
claims.falsifier: Independent recoding of the 13 records places the narrowings at other transitions, for example at cue-to-stimulus measurement.

claims.title: Four claims under one name: the Big Bang
claims.claim: The name “Big Bang” bundles four claims of four warrant grades: the universe expands (observed), it was hot and dense (strong multi-route inference), there was a singularity (a model extended past its validity), and something came from nothing (metaphysics).
claims.falsifier: One observation or inference route supports all four components at the same grade.

claims.title: Species-specific scientific access
claims.claim: Human science is species-specific in its access conditions, which are sensory-cognitive, instrumental, representational and communal; access to formal validity is itself bodily, inscriptional and communal; and objectivity is achieved by disciplined, public control of mediation, not by escaping it.
claims.falsifier: A scientific result reaches the community with its content and warrant through no sensory, instrumental, notational or communal step.

claims.title: Alignment scores: generative sources vs measurement layer
claims.claim: A representational-alignment score depends on two generative sources (a shared target and a shared route) and on a measurement layer (gallery, correspondence, layer rule, statistic). An association statistic over a chosen item population cannot attribute convergence to either source.
claims.falsifier: A general result shows that mutual-kNN or CKA scores are invariant to gallery composition for systems that share a latent structure but allocate precision differently.

claims.title: Paradigms as epistemic sensory ecologies
claims.claim: A scientific paradigm is a stabilized perceptual regime of three jointly necessary parts (calibration and access regimes, trained discrimination, communal validation standards), and paradigm change is typed by which vertex of an E/Os/Oi triangle moved first.
claims.counts_against: Raters cannot assign historical cases a first-moving vertex with inter-rater agreement, or the three components change independently without paradigm change.

claims.title: Access map and access partition
claims.claim: An access procedure defines a map from world states to access products; the states it cannot tell apart form equivalence classes, no processing of its output splits those classes, and splitting a class requires a new coupling to the world.
claims.falsifier: The proposition is proved. Its application fails if a purely computational step, with no new coupling, distinguishes two states that the original access map sends to the same output.

claims.title: Route vs instrument substitution signatures
claims.claim: Under route substitution, a shared target predicts that a named, calibrated relation survives every route change given preserved competence, while an Umwelt source predicts selective change in one pre-named relation with a stable negative control; instrument substitutions move the score under every explanation and cannot separate them.
claims.counts_against: Route substitutions that keep competence intact but weaken a calibrated relation count against the shared-target explanation for that relation. An unchanged relation under a pre-named constraint change, with the control stable, counts against that Umwelt constraint.

claims.title: Alignment clusters are built, not sampled
claims.claim: Alignment clusters between artificial networks and brains are products of niche construction. People built the images, categories and benchmarks the systems train on, and these pass across model generations by ecological inheritance. Measuring constraints where systems are found conditions on a variable those systems helped produce.
claims.counts_against: Alignment clusters neither tighten nor show hysteresis across successive model generations trained on increasingly model-influenced data.

claims.title: Measurement noise as access diagnostic
claims.claim: Residual measurement error that covaries with features of the access system (observer, instrument, laboratory, calibration state or pipeline) is evidence about where mediation enters a result, and it is modeled as such rather than averaged away.
claims.counts_against: In some measurement domain, residuals correlate with access variables, yet modeling that correlation never changes calibration, attribution or the stated result.

claims.title: Access profile with decision-theoretic access
claims.claim: Access to a target contrast is the improvement in expected decision performance over a no-observation baseline; access profiles sharing a target are ordered by Blackwell garbling, and profiles with different estimands are comparable only through a justified bridge.
claims.falsifier: In a benchmark, two routes that the profile marks as Blackwell-ordered on a shared target yield decision performance ordered opposite to the garbling relation.

claims.title: Two-stage alignment test with calibrated estimand
claims.claim: A two-stage design with criteria fixed in advance separates measurement adequacy from source attribution. Stage one holds trained systems fixed and varies only the measurement layer, and stage two varies data provenance, task constraint and inductive bias as separate factors while tracking competence independently.
claims.counts_against: q stays invariant to every evaluation factor (all θ_j = 0 within 95% intervals) and to every route substitution at overlapping competence; then the attribution problem does not arise for q. If q fails stage one, attribution through that pipeline loses its justification.

claims.title: The realist step in the Platonic Representation Hypothesis
claims.claim: The realist reading of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis passes through one step, from statistics of observations to statistics of the world, which its authors prove only for bijective, deterministic observation; the reported scores estimate an evaluation-batch quantity that the theorem never connects to its training distribution.
claims.falsifier: A demonstration shows that, under realistic lossy observation, the learned kernel still identifies world statistics, and evaluation-batch scores consistently estimate the training kernel.

claims.title: Target Priority Principle and the typed target-to-claim graph
claims.claim: Claim-bearing data do not precede target individuation: a scientific claim is the terminal node of a typed dependency graph in which every load-bearing edge carries a target-continuity status (preserved, transformed with bridge, replaced, unresolved).
claims.counts_against: Inter-auditor reliability is too low to reproduce target nodes, edge types and continuity statuses. Or the graph detects no more target drift, shortcut learning or aggregation mismatch than provenance or construct-validity review.

claims.title: Error inheritance: downstream correctness cannot repair upstream misindividuation
claims.claim: If an early assignment maps two world states that differ in the claim-relevant target to the same labelled data, every downstream stage without independent target evidence yields identical output distributions, so no downstream analysis can separate the correct target from the wrong one.
claims.counts_against: The formal core follows from the data-processing inequality. The empirical test fails if, in audited pipelines, located cut points do not predict where external validation fails.

claims.title: Cross-target validation as a third level of objectivity
claims.claim: When target identity is disputed, objectivity requires cross-target validation, testing whether a claim survives live alternative target partitions or receiver models, in addition to within-route and cross-route validation.
claims.counts_against: A retrospective case series in which claims that passed cross-route but not cross-target validation fail no more often than claims that passed both.

claims.title: Target-space conservatism hypothesis
claims.claim: The capacity to register relations grows faster than the capacity to formulate targets, so early uses of a new instrument deepen established target classes, and major conceptual advances coincide with target reconstruction.
claims.falsifier: In instrument histories or data-intensive fields, target repertoires (ontologies, annotation schemas, claim types) diversify as fast as registered distinctions from the first uses of the instrument.

claims.title: Perceptual pointability predicts definitional disputes in science
claims.claim: Scientific disputes over what counts as one instance concentrate on concepts whose referents human perception does not deliver as bounded, cohesive and persisting objects and that no instrument has converted into such objects.
claims.falsifier: With a validated dependent variable, randomly sampled concepts show no negative association between pointability score and definitional-dispute rate. Or disputes persist unchanged after an instrument makes a referent bounded and trackable.

claims.title: Relation-retention profile of a narrowing step
claims.claim: Each load-bearing transition in a scientific route is described by a vector, not a scalar: claim-relative risk reduction G(C), foreclosure L(A) for each live alternative, relation-space contraction K, reversibility V, and target status.
claims.counts_against: Audits that record the profile detect no more foreclosed live alternatives or irreversible preprocessing steps than audits without it.

claims.title: Inherited, constructed and recursive narrowing
claims.claim: Scientific access passes through three narrowings: inherited (evolved and developmental organization of detectable, integrated and salient differences), constructed (target, coupling, pipeline, model, claim) and recursive (earlier outputs reused as upstream conditions without reconsidering the original selection).
claims.counts_against: A recursive-narrowing audit of reused classifications, observer models or benchmarks finds later agreement explained by independent contact with the target as often as by common descent.

claims.title: Objectivity as delta-robust invariance across independent access procedures
claims.claim: A result is objective to the degree that it stays within a declared tolerance delta across calibrated access procedures that share no component, after translation into a common format.
claims.falsifier: Procedures that share no audited component converge within delta on results later overturned at a rate no lower than procedures that share components.

claims.title: The regress stops where routes run out, not where evidence runs out
claims.claim: Route substitution, the operation that separates target from route throughout science, needs more than one route, so the question whether a target exists independent of all experience admits no direct comparison and no discriminating experiment.
claims.falsifier: A measurement procedure gives a different outcome depending on whether an experience-independent target exists, all else held equal.

claims.title: Receiver-class bounded invariance (RCBI) as a rival explanation of scientific success
claims.claim: We propose receiver-class bounded invariance as a rival to the no-miracles argument: measurement-heavy science succeeds because its practices stabilise invariances within practice-fixed uncertainty inside human receiver-instrument systems, then extend them across human receiver classes.
claims.counts_against: A class of novel predictive successes cannot be traced to any previously stabilised invariance or calibration chain. That would favour the truth-based explanation over RCBI.

claims.title: Classical action-world
claims.claim: Organism-scale perception is tuned to decohered, redundantly recorded regularities, so it maps a classical action-world: the overlap of what decoherence makes publicly accessible and what embodiment exploits.
claims.falsifier: Perceptual systems reliably exploit variables that the environment does not record redundantly.

claims.title: Error-relative corroboration
claims.claim: Agreement among routes corroborates an endpoint claim only against a named error, and only when the joint result discriminates the target account from that error by a feature not produced by the disputed pathway.
claims.counts_against: Routes that discriminate a named error only by a feature the disputed pathway produces still reliably predict later adjudication.

claims.title: Measurement requires methodological realism, not physicalism
claims.claim: Measurement commits the investigator to methodological realism only; scientific realism, structural realism and physicalism are three further independent commitments, and the default slide from the first to the last is where the method’s success is silently credited to an ontology.
claims.falsifier: An argument shows that a working measurement practice requires physicalism, not only methodological realism.

claims.title: Four layers of standpoint dependence ordered by correctability
claims.claim: Standpoint dependence in measurement has four layers ordered by correctability: unit choice, instrument bias, species-specific accessibility and conceptual framing; calibration removes the second, reduces the third and leaves the fourth untouched.
claims.falsifier: Calibration alone changes which quantity a field measures. That would place framing inside calibration’s reach and break the ordering.

claims.title: Umwelt-stability is mistaken for reality
claims.claim: Humans take Umwelt-stability for reality because Umwelt regularities are reliable across individuals, developmentally entrenched, and preserved under instrumental extension.
claims.counts_against: Regularities that lack one of the three properties (for example, not preserved under instrumentation) are judged as ‘real’ as often as those that have all three.

claims.title: Three statuses of a framework: method, research programme, metaphysical proposal
claims.claim: A framework is a method if it only demands a specified access chain; it is a research programme if it changes the unit of analysis, causal model and predictions, and a metaphysical proposal if it also changes what counts as fundamental.
claims.counts_against: Applied to real comparative data, the structure card cannot tell a partition change from a sensitivity change.

claims.title: Declared normalization frame for cross-system comparison
claims.claim: Any comparison between systems requires a declared normalization frame; when none is declared, the frame defaults silently to the observer’s own system, as the Earth-orbit year does for cosmic history.
claims.counts_against: Across gravitating systems spanning several decades in mean density, relaxation-state indicators align no better in dynamical times than in years.

claims.title: Class-specific integration windows (Unified Perceptual Field)
claims.claim: Temporal integration windows are selectable traits, and their calibration by stimulus class splits an organism’s perceptual field into long-integration stable segments and short-integration dynamic segments.
claims.falsifier: Integration windows are uniform across stimulus classes within a species, or their between-class differences track phylogeny alone once temperature and body size are controlled.

claims.title: Cosmic time as a stack of measurement layers
claims.claim: Humanity’s measured span of cosmic time grew because instruments added measurement layers, and telescopes extend the celestial-cue extraction that animals already use for navigation.
claims.counts_against: A documented extension of inferred cosmic age that came from theory alone, with no new measurement layer.

claims.title: Hierarchical adiabatic framing of nested gravitating systems
claims.claim: When ε = t_dyn(x)/t_evo(x+1) ≪ 1, a level-x gravitating system relaxes adiabatically inside the quasi-static potential of its host, and ε indexes this separation across star, galaxy, group and cluster levels.
claims.falsifier: Adiabatic invariants of subsystems are poorly conserved in systems with small measured ε, or conserved equally well at ε near one.

claims.title: Temporal processing as a selected trait
claims.claim: Selection shapes each species’ temporal processing, and that processing in turn biases which behaviours and niches the lineage can exploit.
claims.counts_against: Temporal-resolution traits show no association with niche shifts or diversification once body size, temperature and phylogeny are controlled.

claims.title: Cross-species alignment in Θ
claims.claim: Cross-species sensory temporal-resolution data align better in Θ than in seconds when τ_sens is set by 1/CFF or by an allometric metabolic mapping fitted on separate species.
claims.falsifier: Normalisation fails to reduce dispersion beyond a single global rescaling, the gain vanishes on held-out species, or restricted τ models succeed only by becoming per-species fits.

claims.title: Structural convergence at equal internal dynamical age
claims.claim: At fixed halo mass, halos that have lived more internal dynamical times since their last major merger show lower scatter in NFW concentration, with each halo’s clock set by the mean density inside its own scale radius.
claims.falsifier: Concentration scatter at fixed mass does not fall with internal dynamical age, or internal age adds no predictive power beyond formation redshift.

claims.title: Quasi-virialisation of collisionless systems
claims.claim: A collisionless self-gravitating system free of continued violent disturbance reaches quasi-virial equilibrium within about ten crossing times.
claims.falsifier: A mature, isolated collisionless system that keeps non-virial kinematics with no external cause.

claims.title: Disk galaxies saturate after a fixed number of orbits
