claims.claim: Disk galaxy morphology and bar strength reach a stable, saturated state after about 10–20 internal orbital periods at a characteristic radius, independent of galaxy mass.
claims.falsifier: Bar strength, disk thickness or bulge-to-disk ratio keep trending with N_orb above 20 in matched samples.

claims.title: Commensurate nested cycles
claims.claim: Cycles at adjacent levels (atomic, biological, planetary, galactic) lock at commensurate ratios, so geological and biological cycles correlate with astronomical cycles at those ratios.
claims.falsifier: Cycle ratios across levels show no excess of commensurability over the random null.

claims.title: Flow continuity fails when scale separation fails
claims.claim: Where ε_x ≪ 1 is violated, a smooth time-flow description loses explanatory power and dynamics appear punctuated and multi-scale.
claims.falsifier: A system with ε near 1 that stays well described by one smooth timescale.

claims.title: Floor and sky: scale position fixes matter and space
claims.claim: Each system registers processes much faster and smaller than its own reference scale as stable matter and processes much slower and larger as a fixed sky.
claims.falsifier: No growth of measurement error with the rate gap, and no collapse under scale-matched clocks.

claims.title: Operational time as stitched layer clocks
claims.claim: An operational duration is a tick count against a reference timescale defined at a chosen layer, so comparing durations across systems requires a declared normalisation layer.
claims.counts_against: No principled τ family outperforms flexible fitting, or the smoothness of chronometric fields does not depend on the chosen layer.

claims.title: Constructed time Θ and the speed-versus-shape criterion
claims.claim: An organism’s effective time coordinate is Θ(t) = ∫dt/τ(t); if a context changes only τ, behavioural trajectories coincide in Θ, so any residual shape difference marks changed dynamics rather than changed speed.
claims.falsifier: Shape differences persist after Θ normalisation, or different contexts require different best-fitting τ functions.

claims.title: LLM structural-ladder convergence trial
claims.claim: A pre-registered, prompt-blinded trial tests whether models from two providers produce ordered cosmic and experiential structural ladders that align beyond shuffled, reversed and unrelated controls.
claims.counts_against: Alignment does not beat the controls under the pre-declared thresholds.

claims.title: Constructed-time toy simulation
claims.claim: In a toy simulation whose data are generated by a τ-rescaling model, a Level-1 constructed-time model recovers the rescaling in leave-one-context-out validation.
claims.counts_against: None: the gain follows from the simulation design, so the run cannot refute the claim.

claims.title: Complete self-representation has two bottlenecks: acquisition and computation
claims.claim: Complete self-representation requires two separate achievements, acquiring and certifying a complete specification of initial state and dynamics, and computing the target state from it; Wolpert’s lemma establishes the second and FGL constrain the first.
claims.falsifier: A construction inside Wolpert’s framework that endogenously acquires and certifies the complete w_0 required for self-simulation, with a demonstrated correspondence to the completeness FGL exclude.

claims.title: Nested receivers in quantum measurement
claims.claim: Quantum measurement is a layered chain of record formation through six receiver classes, each with its own success criterion; the framework addresses record-basis selection and record efficacy, not unique outcomes.
claims.counts_against: Reduced receiver signatures fail to predict readout behaviour across detector implementations, leaving only a clarifying scheme.

claims.title: Four regimes of self-representation: cell, route and bridge
claims.claim: Every self-representation claim occupies one cell of a timing (synchronous or delayed) by completeness (complete or partial, relative to a pre-declared state space) plane, and two further layers set its standing: construction route and an explicit evidential bridge.
claims.counts_against: A proof that timing and completeness are not independent under a fixed state space; or auditors using the triple show no gain in agreement, or in detecting substituted state spaces, over auditors using careful prose.

claims.title: Single-core multi-port perception
claims.claim: One inferential core coupled to several sensory ports out-predicts independent per-port models per unit complexity and shows cross-port compensation proportional to port precision.
claims.falsifier: Per-port agents match single-core agents in fitness at matched complexity, or compensation is not precision-proportional.

claims.title: Shared-core / local-overlay architecture
claims.claim: Under incomplete local access, a shared inferential core with agent-specific overlays out-predicts fully local models at moderate-to-high task overlap, until coordination cost or common-mode failure cost exceeds the gain.
claims.falsifier: Fully local models match or beat shared-core models at high overlap with low coordination cost.

claims.title: Layer-conservation gradient in rendered perception
claims.claim: Shared lower perceptual layers are more conserved across taxa than higher layers, which become progressively taxon-specific.
claims.falsifier: Higher perceptual layers are as conserved across taxa as lower ones, or more conserved, in matched comparative data.

claims.title: Receiver-category test for detectors
claims.claim: With prepared input fixed and detector implementations varied, a pre-specified receiver-category signature predicts readout class beyond source-only and device-specific models.
claims.falsifier: Full detector models absorb the effect, same-category devices do not cluster, or category effects vanish out of sample.

claims.title: FGL no-go and Wolpert self-simulation reconciled
claims.claim: The conflict between the Fields–Glazebrook–Levin (2024) no-go theorems and Wolpert’s (2025) self-simulation lemma dissolves on three distinctions: generic versus special systems, inductive versus constructed self-models, and fixed versus delay-grown capacity.
claims.falsifier: A case that satisfies FGL’s hypotheses and that Wolpert’s construction also covers without delay.

claims.title: Completeness is indexed to a state space fixed before the evidence
claims.claim: A self-representation is complete only relative to a state space Σ and precision ε declared before the evidence is examined, and narrowing Σ after inspection changes the claim’s regime instead of completing it.
claims.falsifier: A representation shown complete only under a post hoc Σ supports the same predictions and interventions as one complete under a pre-declared Σ.

claims.title: Receiver-dependent selectivity
claims.claim: Every record-forming receiver has a coupling profile, a sensitivity range, a set of stable distinctions and a record threshold, so the form of a record depends in part on the receiver’s organisation.
claims.counts_against: Standard detector models absorb all receiver dependence with no residual category-level regularity.

claims.title: Record versus cue
claims.claim: A record is the stabilised state formed at one stage of the measurement chain, and a cue is the role that state plays for a later receiver, so downstream receivers inherit records rather than the upstream event.
claims.falsifier: A downstream receiver’s output depends on the upstream event beyond what the inherited record carries.
